name: Hibiki Records
description: A quiet, dark store theme for a small independent record shop at the end of a narrow lane in Sakanoue-cho, Minase City, selling second-hand and new vinyl (jazz, ambient, folk, city pop by fictional artists) and a few care accessories, with one bookable listening booth at the back and WooCommerce templates styled to match. Charcoal pages, graphite panels, bone text and a muted grey-teal kept to fine groove rings and rules, with a paler teal for links and labels; Familjen Grotesk for display and text, Martian Mono for catalogue numbers, labels and the ticker. A slim dark bar with a hairline rule: groove mark and wordmark left, the menu, a server-side Open now chip, account and cart right; on phones wordmark, Menu and cart on one line (H1). The home page opens with one quiet line (Records, played slowly) and a record-crate mosaic of square sleeves in mixed sizes (a 2x2 feature, a 2x1 shelf crop, small sleeves), each with a Martian Mono catalogue number; the disc edge peeks out on hover (L8). Then new arrivals, the listening booth, shop details and hours and the journal. The footer opens with a slow, pauseable now-playing ticker band (still for reduced motion), then the shop card and slim links (F5). New arrivals, Listening booth (booking request form), The shop, Journal, Newsletter and Contact. Shop details are edited once in Appearance > Shop details; the booth terms and the grading + shipping note are synced patterns (WooCommerce optional: without it the shop shows static sleeve cells and orders go by email).
deviation: Codes: none (H1 + F5 + L8 as planned; combination unused: Hanabi Matsuri H1/F5/L9, Engawa Works H9/F5/L6, Hamono Kaji H6/F5/L11, Menya Kaen H7/F5; L8 in Aizome Shoten, Kami no Ne, Kami Salon, Hana Kago, Yohaku Studio, Koke Garden with other headers; neighbours #18 Shiori Review H5/F8/L3 oat light and #20 Kage Gallery H4/F3/L9 grey light share no code or palette family). Palette as planned (charcoal #17191A, graphite #262A2B, bone #E6E3DD, muted grey-teal #5C8A86) with added colours, all AA-checked: bone is 13.8:1 on charcoal and 11.3:1 on graphite; grey-teal is 4.6:1 on charcoal but 3.8:1 on graphite (fails 4.5:1), so it is used only for groove rings, rules, dots and marks, never for text; pale teal #8DB5AF was added for links, catalogue numbers and small labels (7.9:1 on charcoal, 6.5:1 on graphite, 7.1:1 on the #1E2122 cells); warm grey #A9A69F for secondary text (7.3:1 on charcoal, 6.0:1 on graphite, 6.5:1 on cells); deep graphite #1E2122 for form fields and cells and a hairline #3A3F40 (decorative, 1.7:1). Buttons are bone with charcoal text (13.8:1), pale teal with charcoal text on hover (7.9:1). H1 differs from Hanabi (festival poster bar), Shashin (film strip), Kissaten (coffee bar) and the washi split bars as a slim charcoal bar with a hairline rule, a groove-ring mark, a Martian Mono sub-line and a server-side Open now chip. F5 differs from Engawa (concrete ticker), Hamono, Menya and Hanabi (poster marquee) as a quiet graphite now-playing band in small Martian Mono at about 14 px/s (60 s minimum per loop), paused on hover/focus, with a Pause button, still under reduced motion. L8 differs from Aizome (book covers), Yohaku (crop marks), Hana Kago (pressed flowers), Koke and Kami as a record crate of square sleeves (2x2 feature, 2x1 shelf crop, 1x1 sleeves) with Martian Mono catalogue numbers and a disc edge that rises on hover. Fonts verified against google/fonts OFL.txt: Familjen Grotesk and Martian Mono are OFL-1.1 without a Reserved Font Name, so both ship as Latin WOFF2 subsets (Familjen Grotesk variable 400-600, 18 KB; Martian Mono width 100, weights 400-500, 15 KB). Single sources: shop details are a theme option (Appearance > Shop details) rendered by one dynamic block in the header chip, ticker, footer, Home, Listening booth, The shop and Contact; booth terms (Listening booth full, home teaser short) and the grading + shipping note (product page short, New arrivals short, Contact full) are synced patterns. Added a newsletter page because check-themes requires it; industry record-shop and page tags listening-booth and new-arrivals are new (The shop reuses the about tag).
